originalTitle: Polls close in South Carolina, where Republicans brace for runoff in race to replace Lindsey Graham – live
summary: Race includes late US senator’s sister, Darline Graham, who was sworn in as interim senator last month; polls also close in Vermont as handful of states hold primaries
content: In Alabama, voters are participating in a second primary this year after the state’s Republican-controlled state legislature reconfigured four of the state’s seven districts after the Supreme Court dismantled a key section of the 1965 Voting Rights Act. In Connecticut, Democratic governor Ned Lamont is seeking a third term, but is facing a challenge from Josh Elliott, the deputy speaker of the state House, who has said Lamont has been ineffective at raising taxes on the rich. The special Republican senate primary is an odd one. Lindsey Graham had already won the Republican primary election for his seat, so the Republican party must hold a special election to replace him on the ballot in November’s general election. The timeline is brutal by American political standards, holding an election within a few weeks of the vacancy. The winner will face Annie Andrews, the Democratic nominee and a pediatrician, in the November general election. Lindsey Graham’s sister Darline Graham had the recommendation of Donald Trump to serve as McMaster’s Senate appointee, and has the president’s endorsement in the primary as well. She has spent decades as a public administrator and disability advocate, serving as the commissioner of the South Carolina commission for the blind from 2019 to 2026. She also has her brother’s considerable state political apparatus behind her. Trump’s endorsement is important, but it is not decisive, according to Frank Tiller, the chair of the Spartanburg county Republican party. “It’s very important, but a lot of people are saying Donald Trump does not know South Carolina politics,” Tiller said. “South Carolina politics is different from a lot of places. Everybody here is fiercely independent.” The compressed election cycle complicates the retail politics South Carolina voters have grown accustomed to, Tiller said. “There are not enough people that know the candidates. Everybody’s calling around trying to find out who to vote for, because they don’t know the candidates.” Aside from Graham, two of the most able Republican competitors for the seat boast substantial campaign infrastructure of their own. Norman has served in the US House of Representatives since 2017, in a district covering the southern suburbs of Charlotte, North Carolina. He is a wealthy real estate developer and a prominent member of the House Freedom caucus. Norman ran unsuccessfully for South Carolina governor earlier this year, and while he did not advance to the runoff, the infrastructure of his campaign was still largely intact when Graham died. Fry represents Myrtle Beach and South Carolina’s conservative eastern border. Fry, an attorney, rose from the ranks of South Carolina’s state legislature after successfully challenging then US representative Tom Rice in the GOP primary in 2022. Rice was one of 10 House Republicans who voted to impeach Trump after the January 6 insurrection. Trump paid him back by endorsing Fry and campaigning to replace Rice. Both Fry and Norman have campaigned as fiscal hawks, highlighting culture war issues. Sanford is a household name in South Carolina politics as a former governor with two separate stints in the US House. Sanford briefly challenged Trump in the 2020 Republican presidential primaries, and made headlines as governor after disappearing from the state for a week, ostensibly on an Appalachian Trail hiking trip, when he was instead having an extramarital affair in Argentina. In South Carolina, all eyes are on the special Republican Senate primary to determine who will succeed the late senator Lindsey Graham. Darline Graham, who was appointed as the replacement to serve the remainder of her brother’s term, is running in the contest with the backing of Donald Trump. If no candidate wins an overall majority of votes, the top two will advance to a runoff on 25 August. Polling suggests that this is the most likely outcome. ICE plans to spend up to $20m to purchase thousands of gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks for officers and agents by March, according to a notice published Monday by the Department of Homeland Security. The devices, called Glove (Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter), are manufactured by Compliant Technologies LLC of Lexington, Kentucky. According to the manufacturer, “the discomfort associated with the stimulation is usually effective in bringing individuals into compliance in less than three seconds and leaves no burns, marks or scars”. The company has advertised the device as a “humane, low-optics, de-escalation solution for many situations facing our men and women in uniform”. The gloves have previously been used in settings such as jails in the US. Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy project director on policing at the American Civil Liberties Union, told the Associated Press that she questioned the use of the devices for civil immigration enforcement. “ICE spent the last year showing this country they are too quick to use force. Now they will be able to deploy electric shocks with the slight push of a button that maybe nobody else can see them do,” she said. “Introducing gloves that can so easily be used to deliver terrible pain in encounters is a recipe for harm to the public.” The Trump administration has issued a new rule barring Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (Chip) programs from funding gender-affirming care for transgender youth. Donald Trump also announced the new restrictions on his Truth Social platform. The programs, meant for low-income children and youth, will not longer cover puberty blockers, hormones and surgical operations – which are rare among minors. The move is the latest move in the administration’s efforts to deny gender-affirming care. “Every young person is entitled to the healthcare that they, their parents and their medical providers agree that they need, without politicians interfering with these important and highly personal decisions. chineseTitle: 南卡罗来纳州民意调查结束，共和党人准备在接替林赛·格雷厄姆的竞选中进行决选——现场直播
chineseSummary: 种族包括已故美国参议员的妹妹达琳·格雷厄姆(Darline Graham)，她上个月宣誓就任临时参议员；佛蒙特州的民意调查也结束，少数州举行初选
chineseContent: 在阿拉巴马州，最高法院废除了 1965 年投票权法案的一个关键部分，共和党控制的州立法机构对该州七个选区中的四个进行了重新配置，选民今年将参加第二次初选。在康涅狄格州，民主党州长内德·拉蒙特正在寻求第三次连任，但面临州众议院副议长乔什·埃利奥特的挑战，埃利奥特表示拉蒙特在提高对富人的税收方面效率不高。共和党参议院特别初选是一件奇怪的事情。林赛·格雷厄姆已经赢得了共和党初选的席位，因此共和党必须举行特别选举来取代他在11月大选中的选票。按照美国的政治标准，这个时间表是残酷的，在空缺后的几周内举行选举。获胜者将在 11 月大选中面对民主党候选人兼儿科医生安妮·安德鲁斯 (Annie Andrews)。林赛·格雷厄姆的妹妹达琳·格雷厄姆得到了唐纳德·特朗普的推荐，担任麦克马斯特的参议员任命，并且在初选中也得到了总统的支持。她几十年来担任公共行政人员和残疾人权益倡导者，并于 2019 年至 2026 年担任南卡罗来纳州盲人委员会专员。她背后还有她哥哥相当大的州政治机构支持。斯帕坦堡县共和党主席弗兰克·蒂勒表示，特朗普的支持很重要，但并不是决定性的。 “这非常重要，但很多人都说唐纳德·特朗普不了解南卡罗来纳州的政治，”蒂勒说。 “南卡罗来纳州的政治与很多地方不同。这里的每个人都非常独立。”压缩的选举周期使零售政治变得复杂
